brief: Nomura's September NFP preview expects payrolls at 130k (after August's 162k, with modest upward revision likely) and the unemployment rate at 4.0%, down from 4.1% and the lowest since January 2025, though risk is skewed toward an unchanged reading. The 4.0% call is below consensus, driven by improving fundamentals (falling layoffs, stronger ADP, claims at a post-2023 low, survey employment indices at multiyear highs, rising job openings) plus a September seasonal pattern: since 2010 the unemployment rate has surprised down about 12bp on average and missed-low in 11 of 16 years, which Nomura attributes to unemployment-to-nonparticipation flows tied to the start of the school year. AHE growth is expected to slow to 0.2% m/m, partly a calendar artifact. A resilient report should keep the Fed focused on inflation. Separately, TPS expirations are a competing drag: Haiti's lapse weighed on education/health hiring, but El Salvador's TPS survived its September 9 deadline, so no major drag is expected there, though deadline uncertainty may have caused frontloading; construction hiring, aided by data-center build-out, could offset Salvadoran-worker exposure. Nomura sees unemployment falling gradually to 3.9% by year-end 2027.
